scientific_interpretation: Restoring nonnegativity materially tightens the degree-three local-order relaxation: the static K3 convex candidate classes safely eliminate wrong final stages A and B on the already-spent ABCD Pythia-14M target, whereas the previous affine superset eliminated none. Therefore the affine failure was partly relaxation looseness rather than solely missing active-transition information. Static K3 remains insufficient to certify the true final stage because wrong stage C and true stage D both survive. No true-chronology claim is made because the degree-three model omits degree-four interaction structure and no omitted-interaction tail bound is available.
methodological_consequence: retain nonnegative K3 convex pruning as a first certified layer and apply the exact interaction-order lift or another active-transition-preserving refinement only to the surviving C/D ambiguity set
